subject: Workplace Skills
title: Deciding With Incomplete Information
description: A quick, practical guide to Deciding With Incomplete Information.

hook.text: Colin Powell's rule: make the call with 40% to 70% of the information. Below 40% is reckless; above 70% is too late.

buildup.text: Waiting for perfect information guarantees missed windows. By the time you have all the data, the opportunity passed.

discovery.text: Good decisions combine available data with judgment. Your pattern recognition fills in gaps that data alone can't.

twist.text: The cost of indecision is often higher than the cost of a wrong decision. Wrong decisions can be corrected.

climax.text: Ask: what's the cost of waiting one more week? If it's high, decide now with what you have. Course-correct later.

punchline.text: Perfect data arrives too late. Decide and adjust.

quiz.question: According to the Powell rule, what's the ideal information range for decision-making?
